stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and features acceleration via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Apple will limit Mac disk access as AI agents ‘substantially’ increase risk
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Apple is introducing new limitations on 'full disk access' for Macs.
The change is a direct response to security risks posed by increasingly capable AI agents.
The new controls aim to ensure users intentionally grant this high level of application access.

stories.title: US arrests tech CEO accused of smuggling $300M in Nvidia chips into China
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A US tech CEO has been arrested in connection with smuggling $300M worth of Nvidia chips into China.
The incident highlights ongoing and persistent challenges regarding the export control and illicit trade of advanced AI hardware.
This case underscores the geopolitical tensions surrounding high-end semiconductor technology between the US and China.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI, indicating its primary function.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the current LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation and utilizes standard ML libraries like transformers and safetensors.
Indicates ongoing community interest and benchmarking activity around Meta's Llama family of models.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML tags such as 'transformers', 'llama', and 'text-generation'.
This indicates ongoing community interest and benchmarking activity around Meta's latest large language models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for persistent AI agents.
The model is designed for complex, multi-step tasks requiring context gathering and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million.
The funding round includes notable investors such as Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama is rapidly gaining traction, serving 8.9 million developers.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31.
The performance boost is achieved on Apple Silicon using MLX and Multi-Token Prediction (MTP).
Speedup reaches up to 90% when running coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and lower memory usage for LLMs.
The updates also lead to higher quality outputs from the language models running on the platform.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Apple changes full-disk access permissions to curb abuse from AI agents
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Apple is modifying full-disk access permissions to restrict potential misuse by AI agents.
The change addresses concerns over AI agents accessing sensitive user data, such as private messages.
The article highlights a disagreement between Apple and Meta regarding the adequacy of existing regulatory frameworks (like the FDA) to control this access.

stories.title: One Basis to Animate Them All: Gaussian Blendshape Distillation for Real-Time Avatars
stories.author: Ivan Laptev
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck of animating 3D Gaussian avatars, which typically requires costly neural inference.
Proposes GALA (Gaussian Animation via Linear Approximation), a distillation method to replace heavy per-frame neural decoding.
Demonstrates that avatar animation can be effectively approximated using a linear combination of identity-independent blendshapes.

stories.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
stories.author: Muzammal Naseer
bullet_points: Introduces KaliBench, a new fine-grained benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to generate executable commands for real-world cybersecurity tools on Kali Linux.
Addresses a critical gap in current LLM evaluations, which often focus on knowledge or high-level agentic tasks rather than precise CLI command generation.
The benchmark incorporates runtime-free verifiable rewards, allowing for rigorous testing of command syntax and tool invocation accuracy in cybersecurity workflows.

stories.title: VISTA: A Visual Harness for Reasoning in an Interactive World
stories.author: Kaiming He
bullet_points: Introduces VISTA, a new visual harness designed to unlock the reasoning potential of multimodal AI models.
VISTA provides general-purpose multimodal models with long-horizon vision capabilities in interactive environments.
The system features a lossless visual memory allowing the model to actively retrieve and utilize past visual observations.

stories.title: One Basis to Animate Them All: Gaussian Blendshape Distillation for Real-Time Avatars
stories.author: Ivan Laptev
bullet_points: Addresses the high computational cost of animating 3D Gaussian avatars, a technique known for fast rendering.
Introduces GALA (Gaussian Animation via Linear Approximation), a distillation method to replace heavy per-frame neural decoding.
Proposes that avatar animation can be effectively approximated using a linear combination of identity-independent blendshapes.

stories.title: The Missing Primitive: Diagnosing and Repairing Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
stories.author: Zhengzhong Tu
bullet_points: The research addresses the fundamental question of whether LLMs possess genuine structural mathematical understanding, rather than just pattern matching.
It introduces the concept of 'Mathematical Primitive' as a new diagnostic tool to probe the underlying reasoning capabilities of LLMs.
The work aims to systematically diagnose current limitations and leverage these findings to improve LLM performance through post-training methods.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free decision-making based on text input.
Decision models provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scoring.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine, improving functionality on Apple silicon devices.

stories.title: Meta open sources code to let you make Muse AI gadgets
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Meta has open-sourced the code for its Muse AI agent.
This allows users to build custom 'Muse gadgets' using the provided code.
Suggested applications include integrating Muse with E Ink displays or HDMI sticks.

stories.title: Netflix is pivoting away from prestige
stories.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
bullet_points: Netflix is reportedly shifting its content strategy away from high-budget, prestige productions.
This pivot is evidenced by the streamer ending long-term production deals with acclaimed directors.
The move signals a potential strategic change in how Netflix approaches content creation compared to rivals.

stories.title: OpenAI’s Dot agent is enterprise software that can also order your dinner
stories.author: Allison Johnson
bullet_points: OpenAI has unveiled a new agent platform named 'Dots'.
The platform is positioned as enterprise software, capable of performing tasks ranging from professional duties to personal errands like ordering food.
The article contrasts Dots with competitors like Meta Muse, noting Dots' more 'workplace' orientation.

stories.title: Rivian’s sales pop as the company’s big R2 bet starts to pay off
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Rivian reported significant Q3 growth, with production increasing by 85% year-over-year.
Vehicle deliveries saw a strong 45% jump in the third quarter.
The sales increase suggests positive early momentum for Rivian's anticipated more affordable R2 vehicle.

stories.title: Dots get up in Muse’s business
stories.author: Jacob Kastrenakes
bullet_points: OpenAI has released 'Dots,' a new product positioned as a business-focused alternative to Muse.
Dots is a paid service, requiring a minimum subscription of $100 per month.
The product appears to be a more professional, enterprise-oriented version of the creative tools offered by Muse.

stories.title: Amazon’s $1B plan to combat data center backlash draws more backlash
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Amazon's $1B initiative to address data center concerns is facing criticism.
The company received praise for ending Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs).
Amazon is being criticized for minimizing the environmental impact of its data centers.

stories.title: Lyft settles landmark driver misclassification lawsuit for $272.5M
stories.author: Cyrus Farivar
bullet_points: Lyft has settled a major lawsuit concerning the misclassification of its drivers.
The settlement amount reached $272.5 million.
The resolution faces criticism from groups claiming drivers are owed significantly more.

stories.title: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real: Guided Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
stories.author: Haozhi Qi
bullet_points: Introduces RPG (Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real), a framework for autonomous improvement of embodied agents.
The framework allows robots to improve execution skills without requiring updates to the underlying model weights.
RPG leverages offline datasets to construct simulation-based practice tasks using execution feedback.

stories.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
stories.author: Chelsea Finn
bullet_points: Introduces ScholarCatalyst, a new benchmark designed to test AI's ability to find inspirational prior research.
The benchmark leverages expert human knowledge, where researchers annotate which past papers influenced their own work.
This addresses a key gap in current AI research: the ability to sense relevant, buried ideas from vast scientific archives.

stories.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: Introduces SILSA, a new framework for high-resolution 3D generation.
Addresses limitations of current methods (voxel latents/multi-stage pipelines) which fragment surfaces and weaken topology.
Uses compact sliding-window slice latents to maintain topological consistency during 3D shape synthesis.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Introduces Continuous Diffusion Language Models (CDLMs) as an alternative to discrete diffusion models for language generation.
CDLMs aim to overcome the independent token sampling bottleneck found in discrete diffusion models, which hinders bidirectional reasoning.
The core mechanism involves denoising a shared continuous state, allowing for better capture of statistical dependencies among generated tokens.

stories.title: DMAD: Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation for Fast Visual Generation
stories.author: Chongyang Ma
bullet_points: Introduces DMAD (Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation) for faster visual generation.
DMAD reframes distribution matching as a classification task, allowing direct learning of log-density ratios.
It aims to improve upon previous methods that required auxiliary diffusion models, reducing memory and computation costs.

stories.title: Higher-Order Molecular Grammars for Generative and Foundation Models in Chemistry
stories.author: Tolga Birdal
bullet_points: Introduces Higher-order Grammar Representation (HGR) to address limitations in molecular learning models.
HGR is designed to explicitly encode complex, higher-order molecular topologies like ring systems and recurring motifs.
The framework aims to overcome the computational demands and decoding difficulties associated with existing higher-order representations.

stories.title: Embedding Prediction Helps Image Generation
stories.author: Stella X. Yu
bullet_points: The research proposes using predicted embeddings as a conditioning mechanism in diffusion transformers for image generation.
The core technique involves training a Next-Embedding Predictive Autoregression (NEPA) model to forecast the next continuous embedding in a sequence.
This approach leverages the sequential nature of image generation (noisy to clean) to train the predictive model.

stories.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: SILSA introduces a new framework for high-resolution 3D generation using compact sliding-window slice latents.
It addresses limitations in existing methods (voxel latents/multi-stage pipelines) where surface fragmentation and topological inconsistency occur.
The core innovation aims to improve topological consistency and reduce generation costs for complex 3D shapes.

stories.title: TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning
stories.author: Aritra Dutta
bullet_points: TACO introduces a new optimizer designed to reduce the memory overhead associated with full-parameter fine-tuning of Large Language Models (LLMs).
The core innovation is a Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse approach, addressing the memory constraints of large models on current GPUs.
TACO aims to improve upon existing state compression methods, specifically addressing performance degradation seen with alternatives like Muon when fine-tuning AdamW.

stories.title: Cost-augmented Schrödinger bridges on graphs are exactly solvable: a Feynman-Kac tilt replaces learned control
stories.author: Akshay Balsubramani
bullet_points: The research addresses the problem of finding a generalized Schrödinger bridge on graphs that incorporates a state-visitation cost.
A key finding is that the cost-augmented bridge can be solved exactly by utilizing a Feynman-Kac tilt on the reference process.
This exact solution eliminates the need for complex learning methods, such as temporal-difference penalties, previously used to restore the cost.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Introduces Continuous Diffusion Language Models as an alternative to discrete diffusion models for language generation.
Addresses a key limitation of discrete diffusion models: independent token sampling during parallel decoding, which breaks statistical dependencies.
Continuous diffusion models overcome this by denoising a shared continuous state, aiming to maintain inter-token dependencies.

stories.title: Trust the Direction, Search the Step: Zero-and-First-Order Methods for LLM Fine-Tuning
stories.author: Aritra Dutta
bullet_points: Addresses the critical challenge of step-size selection in large-scale LLM fine-tuning.
Introduces Zero-and-First-Order optimization (ZFO) to decouple direction selection from step-size.
ZFO uses a first-order optimizer for direction and zeroth-order evaluations along a 1D subspace for step-size selection.

stories.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
stories.author: Muzammal Naseer
bullet_points: Introduces KaliBench, a new benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to generate executable commands for real-world cybersecurity tools on Kali Linux.
Addresses a critical gap in current LLM evaluations, which often focus on knowledge or high-level tasks rather than precise CLI command generation.
Emphasizes the need for fine-grained evaluation due to the sensitivity of cybersecurity workflows to minor syntax or flag errors.

stories.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
stories.author: Chelsea Finn
bullet_points: Introduces ScholarCatalyst, a new benchmark designed to test the ability of AI to find inspiring prior research.
The benchmark leverages expert human knowledge, where researchers annotate which past papers influenced their current work.
Addresses the challenge of AI systems needing to sense relevant, buried ideas within massive scientific archives.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Introduces Continuous Diffusion Language Models as an alternative to discrete diffusion models for language generation.
Discrete diffusion models suffer from a bottleneck where parallel decoding samples tokens independently, losing statistical dependencies.
Continuous diffusion models address this by denoising a shared continuous state, potentially preserving inter-token dependencies.

stories.title: AutoCompact: Learning When to Compact Context in Long-Horizon Coding Agents
stories.author: Xin Dong
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of managing context in long-horizon coding agents, where early information becomes stale.
Introduces AutoCompact, a method that trains coding agents to dynamically decide when and how to compact their working context.
Focuses on improving the efficiency and coherence of AI agents performing complex, repository-level software engineering tasks.

stories.title: Keyword Harnesses Fail Open: A Cheap Diagnostic Ladder for Tool-Use Claims in Small Language Models
stories.author: Juan S. Santillana
bullet_points: Keyword-matching benchmarks can falsely credit small language models for tool use they do not actually perform.
The paper proposes a 'cheap diagnostic ladder' to rigorously test and validate tool-use claims in LLMs.
The study demonstrates this false positive issue using matched-architecture Spanish security language models.

stories.title: Finetuning with Sampling: SFT Learns Better Than You Think
stories.author: Yilun Du
bullet_points: The paper addresses limitations in post-training techniques (SFT and RL) used to enhance frontier language models.
It challenges the conventional view that RL is superior to SFT for generalization, suggesting SFT might be more capable than assumed.
The core contribution is a new method, 'Finetuning with Sampling,' which aims to improve model capabilities while mitigating known weaknesses of SFT and RL.

stories.title: Argo-Bench: Evaluating Data Agents on Enterprise-Scale Workflows
stories.author: Joseph J Ma
bullet_points: Argo-Bench is a new evaluation framework designed to test 'Data Agents' on complex, real-world enterprise workflows.
It addresses the limitations of existing text-to-SQL benchmarks, which only test query generation and often have flawed answer keys.
The framework uses public datasets to simulate enterprise scenarios requiring reasoning across multiple tables and statistical analysis.

stories.title: Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes
stories.author: Spyros Gidaris
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'Where-OPD,' a method applying on-policy self-distillation to Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
This technique aims to improve MLLM reasoning by using a privileged, potentially self-generated, supervisory signal.
It addresses a gap in current MLLM research, which often limits visual guidance to simple image crops for fine-grained perception.

stories.title: Court agrees with EFF: Utah's VPN law demands a technical impossibility
stories.author: hn_acker
bullet_points: A court ruling supports the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) regarding Utah's VPN law.
The core issue is that the law imposes a technical impossibility on VPN providers.
This highlights ongoing legal and technical conflicts between state regulations and privacy technologies.

stories.title: The Four Horsemen of Agentic Coding
stories.author: distantprovince.substack.com via guillego
bullet_points: The article discusses 'Agentic Coding,' a growing trend in AI development.
It frames the key components or challenges of this paradigm as 'The Four Horsemen.'
The topic suggests a deep dive into the architecture and capabilities of autonomous coding agents.

stories.title: gVisor is being donated to CNCF
stories.author: gvisor.dev via carlana
bullet_points: gVisor, a container sandbox technology, is being donated to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF).
This move signifies a major integration of gVisor into the broader cloud-native ecosystem.
The donation suggests increased standardization and community adoption for gVisor's security features.

stories.title: The More Context You Give Your AI Coding Agent, the Worse It Can Get
stories.author: robertadam987_
bullet_points: Challenges the common advice to always provide extensive context to AI coding agents.
Suggests that over-contextualization can lead to degraded or worse AI performance.
Highlights a nuanced issue in the practical application of AI tools in software development.

stories.title: Building Sarrera: Self-Hosted Enterprise AI Inference Gateway with RBAC, Token Quotas & Telemetry
stories.author: marioezquerro
bullet_points: Details the architecture for building a self-hosted, private AI inference gateway.
Integrates key tools like LiteLLM, Caddy, Langfuse, and Open WebUI for functionality.
Features enterprise-grade controls including Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and token quotas.
